materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 1 of "Arts, Identity, Culture, and Ethics" (unit 5, grade 8) is a diagnostic probe on art and identity without forced disclosure. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Curate an ethical context-rich exhibition or program note set around a question of art and society. Today's work contributes to that by handling art and identity without forced disclosure at the launch and diagnostic stage, against the unit's wider topics of art and identity without forced disclosure, historical and cultural context, representation and stereotype, and appropriation attribution and collaboration. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Before any instruction on art and identity without forced disclosure, make a short baseline response so you can see your own starting point later. Spend a few minutes producing something — a quick sketch, a short pattern, a few bars, a rough plan, or a written description if you prefer not to produce a piece today. Then write three things you already notice about art and identity without forced disclosure and one question you cannot yet answer. Keep this baseline; you will compare later work against it. Nothing here is judged for quality, only for being honest and complete. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about art and identity without forced disclosure, and it belongs to "Arts, Identity, Culture, and Ethics", which also covers separate topics such as historical and cultural context. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about art and identity without forced disclosure; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 8 the bar is independent work that anticipates the obvious objection: name the case most likely to break your result, test it, and report what happened.

Three specific noticings and one open question are recorded in writing.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting art and identity without forced disclosure.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for art and identity without forced disclosure follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for art and identity without forced disclosure, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for art and identity without forced disclosure works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of art and identity without forced disclosure, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking art and identity without forced disclosure mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply art and identity without forced disclosure under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on art and identity without forced disclosure rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
